q: Illuminance is the total luminous flux incident on a surface per unit _____ and is measured in lux.
e: Luminous flux is the visible-light power of a source, measured in lumen. One lumen is 1/683 watt at 555 nm, not at 400 nm. Opaque-solid radiation is a surface effect, not a volume effect.

q: According to the inverse square law of illuminance, the illuminance on a surface is inversely proportional to the _____ of the distance between the source and surface.
e: Illuminance is luminous flux landing per unit area, in lux, and follows E_v = I_v cos theta / r^2. It falls as the square of distance. School reading areas are often quoted near 500 lux. According to the inverse square law of cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: In the illuminance formula $E_v = \frac{I_v \cos \theta}{r^2}$, $\theta$ is the angle between the direction of light and the _____ to the illuminated surface.
e: Illuminance is luminous flux landing per unit area, in lux, and follows E_v = I_v cos theta / r^2. It falls as the square of distance. A wavefront is perpendicular to the rays.
